questions.stem: What is the term used to describe the rotating vector that represents the amplitude and phase of an alternating current or voltage?
questions.solution: The term used to describe the rotating vector that represents the amplitude and phase of an alternating current or voltage is 'phasor'. A phasor is a vector that rotates with angular frequency, capturing both the magnitude and phase of the signal. The other options do not refer to this specific concept; 'vector' is too general, 'magnitude' refers only to size, and 'amplitude' refers only to the maximum value.

hi.stem: एक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा या वोल्टता के आयाम और कला का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले घूमते हुए सदिश के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला शब्द क्या है?
hi.solution: एक प्रत्यावर्ती धारा या वोल्टता के आयाम और कला का प्रतिनिधित्व करने वाले घूमते हुए सदिश के लिए उपयोग किया जाने वाला शब्द 'फेजर' है। एक फेजर एक सदिश होता है जो कोणीय आवृत्ति के साथ घूमता है, जो संकेत के आयाम और कला दोनों को दर्शाता है। अन्य विकल्प इस विशिष्ट अवधारणा के लिए संदर्भ नहीं होते हैं; 'सदिश' बहुत सामान्य है, 'आयाम' केवल आकार के लिए होता है, और 'आवेश' केवल अधिकतम मान के लिए होता है।
hi.critique: Hindi translation accurately reflects the English original in meaning, technical terms, and answer position. 'फेजर' is the correct technical term used in Hindi textbooks.

questions.stem: What is the term used to describe a vector that rotates about the origin with angular speed and represents the sinusoidally varying quantities in an AC circuit?
questions.solution: A phasor is a vector that rotates about the origin with angular speed and is used to represent sinusoidally varying quantities in AC circuits. A vector is a general term for a directed quantity, not specifically related to AC circuits. A rotator is not a standard term in this context. Magnitude refers to the size of a quantity, not a rotating vector.

questions.stem: In an AC circuit, what happens to the power dissipated in a purely inductive or capacitive circuit?
choices: It is equal to the source voltage
It is equal to the current
questions.solution: In a purely inductive or capacitive circuit, the power dissipated is zero because the phase difference between the voltage and current is 90 degrees, making the cosine of the phase angle zero. This results in no real power being dissipated. The other options are incorrect because they do not account for the phase difference.

questions.stem: What is the term used for the effective value of an alternating current?
questions.solution: The term used for the effective value of an alternating current is RMS value. This is because the RMS value is the equivalent direct current value that would produce the same heating effect. Amplitude is the maximum value of the current, peak value is the same as amplitude, and average value is not used for effective comparison.

questions.stem: What is the unit of capacitive reactance?
questions.solution: Capacitive reactance is a measure of opposition to alternating current, and like resistance, it is measured in ohms. Ampere is the unit of current, volt is the unit of electric potential, and farad is the unit of capacitance. Therefore, the correct unit is ohm.

hi.stem: कैपैसिटिव प्रतिघात की इकाई क्या है?
hi.solution: कैपैसिटिव प्रतिघात एल्टरनेटिंग करंट के प्रतिरोध का माप है, और प्रतिरोध के समान इसकी इकाई ओम में मापी जाती है। एम्पियर धारा की इकाई है, वोल्ट विद्युत विभव की इकाई है, और फैराड कैपैसिटेंस की इकाई है। इसलिए सही इकाई ओम है।

questions.stem: If the frequency of the AC source is doubled, what happens to the capacitive reactance?
questions.solution: Capacitive reactance is inversely proportional to frequency, so when the frequency is doubled, the reactance is halved. Doubling the frequency does not double the reactance, nor does it make it infinite or zero, as those outcomes do not align with the inverse relationship between frequency and capacitive reactance.

hi.solution: धारिता प्रतिरोध आवृत्ति के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती होता है, अतः जब आवृत्ति दुगुनी कर दी जाती है, तो प्रतिरोध आधा हो जाता है। आवृत्ति को दुगुना करने से प्रतिरोध को दुगुना नहीं किया जाता है, न ही इसे अनंत या शून्य बना दिया जाता है, क्योंकि ये परिणाम आवृत्ति और धारिता प्रतिरोध के व्युत्क्रमानुपाती संबंध के साथ मेल नहीं खाते हैं।

questions.stem: What is the average power dissipated in a purely capacitive AC circuit?

questions.stem: In a purely inductive AC circuit, how does the current relate to the voltage in terms of phase angle?
choices: Current is in phase with voltage
Current is out of phase with voltage by π
questions.solution: In a purely inductive AC circuit, the current lags the voltage by π/2 because the inductor resists changes in current, causing it to reach its peak after the voltage does. Current leading voltage by π/2 occurs in capacitive circuits, where the capacitor resists changes in voltage. Current being in phase with voltage is characteristic of resistive circuits, not inductive ones. A phase difference of π is not typical for an inductive circuit, as it would imply the current is completely out of sync, which is not the case.

questions.stem: In a purely capacitive AC circuit, the power supplied to the capacitor over a complete cycle is zero. Why is this the case?

questions.solution: The correct option is because the capacitor stores energy and releases it back to the circuit. This happens because during one half-cycle, the capacitor charges and stores energy, and during the other half-cycle, it discharges and returns the energy to the circuit, resulting in zero net power consumption over a full cycle. The other options are incorrect because capacitors do consume energy temporarily, they do allow current to flow, and they are typically connected to the circuit.
